card.meaningEn: Having real importance, value or effect; about the actual content of something, not just its form.
card.howUsed: Common in academic, legal and professional writing to say something is real and meaningful, not surface-level or procedural. In everyday speech people usually say “real” or “meaningful” instead.
patterns: have a substantive discussion about sth
no substantive difference between A and B
examples: The reviewer gave substantive feedback on my methodology, not just grammar fixes.
We need a substantive discussion about the budget before we sign the contract.
After three meetings, there has been no substantive progress on the project.
Version 2 includes substantive changes to the API, so read the release notes.

dontConfuse.difference: large in size, amount or importance: “a substantial increase in cost”.
